artifacts.summary: Admission gate, the two declarations and the per-invocation batch record: what changed, decisions, deviations and verification evidence.

completion_data.completion_summary: orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh now runs an admission gate from the new lib/batch-admission-lib.sh: it refuses worktree_isolation batch (isolation_unimplemented) and, when integration_branch is declared, an off-branch or dirty primary tree; on admit it writes one batch record per invocation under specs/.orchestration/batch/. Both declarations and the record are documented in the standards documents, covered by a new 81-assertion suite and a 28-assertion cycle-plan group, and redeployed.

memory_candidates.content: To keep a long local command alive across several Bash tool calls in a dispatched agent, start it with `setsid nohup bash job.sh > log 2>&1 < /dev/null &` and have job.sh print its own PID as its first line; wait on that PID with a `kill -0` loop under `timeout 160`, in calls kept under about 170 seconds. Plain nohup children die when the starting call returns, and under setsid `$!` is the wrapper, not the job.

A sourced bash library that reports through result variables read only by its caller trips shellcheck SC2034 at -S warning on the last assignment site of each variable; the shellcheck gate accepts an inline `# shellcheck disable=SC2034` with a one-line reason at each flagged assignment, never a file-level disable.

sapience_notes.subject: orchestration admission arming rule
sapience_notes.value: The off-branch and dirty-primary-tree refusals arm only when integration_branch is declared in .claude-extensions.json; an undeclaring repository gets one advisory per session and no refusal. Rationale: the amending decision record (R5 amended, Option L1) says a repository that declares nothing behaves as before, and the task description defers to the record.

sapience_notes.subject: admission state territory
sapience_notes.value: Exactly specs/, .claude-extensions.json and .memory/. Only tracked changes are tested (git diff --name-only HEAD with exclude pathspecs); untracked files never refuse. .memory/ was added to the record's two-member set because memory-retrieval counters dirty it with no task editing it; source-store index-entries.json files are excluded because they are derived from real edits and naming them would put a repository-specific path in a deliverable.

sapience_notes.subject: worktree_isolation: batch
sapience_notes.value: Declared but not implemented. Any declared value other than off (batch, an unknown string, a non-string) stops every /orchestrate invocation with reason isolation_unimplemented, naming batch_worktree_creation_when_isolation_on. This is a deliberate loud exception to the declarations surface's fail-open posture, on the same ground as the unusable closing_gate exception.

sapience_notes.subject: batch record at specs/.orchestration/batch/{session_id}.json
sapience_notes.value: One per invocation by construction: its existence is the first-cycle marker, so later cycles skip the dirty-tree test (the invocation's own dispatches leave dirt) while the branch test still runs every cycle. Never written under --dry-run, on a refusal, or outside a git work tree. The deferred batch-branch name and worktree path arrive later as one additive isolation object; landing_proofs is an append-only array owned by the landing mechanism.

sapience_notes.subject: sync-manifest-scripts.sh --write
sapience_notes.value: It enumerates an extension's scripts with git ls-files, so a newly created, untracked script is invisible and --write reports 0 missing. Running git add -N on the explicit paths first makes it insert the entries.

sapience_notes.subject: suites that sandbox orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh
sapience_notes.value: Three suites, not two, need every newly hard-sourced library staged explicitly: test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, test-orchestrate-unwind-dispatch.sh and test-force-phases.sh. The third overlays source-store copies of individual libraries on a wholesale copy of the DEPLOYED lib directory, so it fails only before a redeploy and a search for explicit library lists misses it.

sapience_notes.subject: test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh
sapience_notes.value: Its fixture is a detached git worktree of HEAD, so it judges committed content, not the working tree: an uncommitted lint fix does not reach it, and it reported shellcheck findings that the live tree no longer had. It passed 17/0 once the fix was committed.
